The submitted answer is (A) circle, and I verified it as correct.

Both arcs have rx = ry = 14.29, so each is a circular arc and the 347.79 rotation has no effect. The chord between the endpoints is √(27.93² + 6.04²) ≈ 28.576, which is almost exactly the diameter, 28.58. The two centers are therefore almost the same point, about 0.5 apart. The two large arcs together sweep slightly more than 2π, which is essentially a full circle. Ellipse (K) would apply only if rx ≠ ry, so circle is the better label.

The attached program printed "CHECK FAIL", but its numbers match this analysis. It found the arcs are circular and the path closes, and its failure line only restates that two same-radius arcs with nearly the same center cover a full circle.

{"pass": true, "reason": "rx = ry = 14.29 and the chord ≈ 28.576 is nearly the diameter 28.58, so the two arcs form a full circle, not a general ellipse."}
